basic_info: 52-year-old patient presenting for annual exam with palpitations, especially when stressed
present_illness: Onset of palpitations recently, associated with stress; no prior evaluation or treatment mentioned. Palpitations occur occasionally, last about a week, triggered by stress, and have not been relieved by meditation or running with the dog. No chest pain or dizziness associated. History of atrial fibrillation, currently in and out of rhythm over the past year. The patient had an event monitor done last month, which showed episodes of atrial fibrillation with conversion pauses. The patient is unsure of the exact frequency and duration of atrial fibrillation episodes and conversion pauses, as noted in the event monitor results from last month. The patient reports that atrial fibrillation episodes typically last for variable durations, with conversion pauses of uncertain length. The patient notes that episodes are often triggered by stress, and there is no clear pattern to their occurrence. The patient has not experienced chest pain or dizziness during these episodes.
past_history: History of rheumatoid arthritis, atrial fibrillation, and reflux. On methotrexate for arthritis. No allergies. Family history of cardiac conditions: unknown.
physical_exam: Vital signs: BP 128/82 mmHg, HR 78 bpm, RR 16, Temp 36.8°C. Cardiac exam: regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs, gallops, or rubs. No jugular venous distension. No peripheral edema. Respiratory exam: clear to auscultation. Abdominal exam: soft, non-tender, no organomegaly. Neurological exam: intact. Skin exam: no rashes or signs of inflammation.
aux_exam: ECG: Normal sinus rhythm, no evidence of atrial fibrillation. Troponin I: 0.03 ng/mL (normal). BNP: 120 pg/mL (elevated). Echocardiogram: Normal left ventricular function, no structural abnormalities. Thyroid function tests: TSH 2.1 mIU/L, free T4 1.2 ng/dL (normal). Event monitor: Shows episodes of atrial fibrillation with conversion pauses (results from last month). Event monitor findings: Frequency of episodes and duration of conversion pauses need clarification from the patient.
